summary: Iteration 6 verified the NEW account-deletion feature end-to-end plus regression. Backend: 38/38 pytest cases pass (34 prior regression + 4 new deletion tests in test_account_deletion.py). New tests validate: (1) DELETE /api/account without a token -> 401, (2) DELETE with garbage bearer -> 401, (3) throwaway user seeded via direct Mongo insert + real onboard/commit + /logs + /tasks; DELETE /api/account returns {ok: true} and MongoDB counts drop to 0 across all 8 user-scoped collections AND user_sessions AND users; the same token subsequently returns 401 on /auth/me and /workspace, (4) per-user isolation — with two throwaway users seeded, deleting user A does not touch user B (user B's users/user_sessions/profile/domains/daily_logs/tasks counts all remain intact, /auth/me still returns 200, /workspace still shows user B's domain). Frontend mobile (390x844): PART1 authenticated fixture user -> profile-button opens Onboarding modal -> delete-account danger link visible -> tapping reveals two-step confirm (both cancel-delete and confirm-delete visible with 'This permanently erases…' copy) -> cancel-delete hides confirm and restores the delete link, and post-cancel /api/workspace still returns 200 with 3 domains (no data lost). PART2 with a throwaway session seeded directly in Mongo, running the full flow (profile-button -> delete-account -> confirm-delete) navigated the app back to the Login screen with 'Continue with Google' visible; the throwaway token then returned 401 from /api/auth/me — confirming the session was invalidated and the local token cleared. PART3 regression smoke on the re-seeded fixture: Companion tab crisis message 'I feel hopeless right now' still renders the SAFETY label and 988 grounding text (no red screen, no console errors beyond the expected 401 during the delete flow). Fixture user re-seeded at end via seed_test_user.py so the fixture token is valid again for future runs.
action_items: OPTIONAL: DELETE /api/account currently returns 200 whether or not any docs existed for the user. Consider returning a small counts summary (e.g. {ok:true, removed: {tasks:3, logs:5, ...}}) so audit logs / support have a paper trail.

OPTIONAL: The danger link 'Delete my account & data' inside the Onboarding modal is visually compact — consider adding a small trash icon and slightly more paddingVertical (currently the touch target is ~28px tall). Not blocking for App Store submission.

OPTIONAL: deleteAccount() in index.tsx swallows API errors and still calls onDeleted?.(). This is a deliberate 'proceed to sign out regardless' — fine, but consider surfacing a toast if the DELETE failed (e.g. offline) so the user knows to retry from a fresh session.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py DELETE /api/account correctly scopes every delete by user_id (loop over 8 collections + user_sessions + users). No cross-user leakage risk — verified by isolation test.
server.py current_user() dependency ensures DELETE requires a valid bearer session; expired/invalid/missing all return 401 before touching the db.

index.tsx line 353 deleteAccount catches api() errors and still triggers onDeleted, and onDeleted (line 40) calls tokenSet('') then setUser(null) — guarantees the app returns to Login even if the network call fails.
index.tsx Onboarding modal uses testIDs delete-account / cancel-delete / confirm-delete matching the review spec exactly.
Confirm copy 'This permanently erases your profile, logs, tasks, reflections, and chats. This cannot be undone.' meets Apple's App Store Review Guideline 5.1.1(v) for an in-app account deletion path.
Fixture token was preserved across the destructive backend tests because the delete tests used a separately-seeded throwaway user + throwaway token (seeded and cleaned up in-fixture).

success_rate.frontend: 3/3 flows — cancel-delete safe path, confirm-delete returns to Login + token invalidated, crisis-safety regression intact

seed_data_creation: Created and destroyed two throwaway MongoDB users during backend tests: user_deletetest01 (used in TestAccountDeletionFlow) and user_isolationtest01 (used in TestAccountDeletionIsolation). For UI testing seeded user_uithrowaway with token test-session-ui-throwaway-0001 which was consumed by the delete-account UI flow (now gone, 401 verified). Fixture user user_testfixture01 with token test-session-lifeos-fixture-0001 was RE-SEEDED at end via /app/backend/seed_test_user.py — safe for main agent smoke tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend URL: https://companion-compass.preview.emergentagent.com. Fixture token still: test-session-lifeos-fixture-0001. Deletion regression lives in /app/backend/tests/test_account_deletion.py — it seeds and cleans up its own throwaway users so it can be run alongside the main suite (all 38 tests together pass in ~33s). The UI delete flow lives inside the Onboarding modal (open via header 'profile-button'), testIDs delete-account -> confirm-delete/cancel-delete; on success index.tsx clears lifeos_token and resets user, dropping the app back to the Login screen ('continue-google' testID). If you re-run the UI delete flow, seed a throwaway session first (see /tmp/seed_throwaway.py from iter6 or reuse the pattern in test_account_deletion.py); do NOT run confirm-delete under the fixture token unless you re-seed after.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs found. DELETE /api/account plus the mobile confirm-flow behave exactly as specified: token invalidated, per-user data wiped across all 8 domain collections + session + users row, isolation preserved for other users, UI returns to Login on success and stays put on cancel.
